narrative: Demand for PL1__M1914E67 is continuous and right-skewed (CV=0.54) with no statistically significant trend over the 130 working-day observation window. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.43), likely reflecting two distinct routing modes, with transport variability as the dominant uncertainty driver. A capacity-constrained (r,Q) policy is recommended: the theoretical EOQ of 6,675 units is capped at 3,060 units by the 3,982-unit storage limit, but this still delivers a 78.2% annual cost reduction over the current SAP policy by eliminating excessive ordering frequency. Safety stock is raised from 421 to 921 units to achieve the 95% service level target.
warnings: High capacity utilization (99.98%): storage cap of 3,981.709 units limits order quantity to 3,060 instead of EOQ 6,675. Consider expanding storage.
Moderate lead time variability (CV=0.43): bimodal distribution suggests two routing modes. Supplier coordination recommended.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (93.1% non-zero days) with no trend, making a fixed reorder-point policy appropriate. EOQ minimises total ordering and holding cost; the MOQ of 506 is well below the EOQ so it does not bind. Capacity constrains the order quantity to 3,060 units but the policy structure remains (r,Q).
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is binding at 99.98% utilisation post-replenishment. Any positive demand shock during a replenishment cycle could cause a stockout that the safety stock cannot absorb. Expanding storage to ~7,600 units would unlock the full EOQ and reduce total annual cost by a further ~30%.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (506) + safety stock (921) = 1,427 units, which is below max_storage_units (3,981.709). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
